headline: South Asia: Ethiopia's Tigray rebels abandon regional capital as govt advances
script:
Good morning. This is your global conflict briefing.

BOTTOM LINE UP FRONT:
- South Asia: Ethiopia's Tigray rebels abandon regional capital as govt advances.
- Western Russia: Russians attack Izium with drones: five injured.
- Persian Gulf Region: IDF targets Yahya Sinwar's successor, Hamas Gaza leader Ali al-Amoudi, in strike.

Full breakdown follows.

NORTH AMERICA
United States - bottom line: Naval Special Warfare Command failed to identify, treat TBI in service members: Watchdog.
- Military Times, 16 hours ago: Naval Special Warfare Command failed to identify, treat TBI in service members: Watchdog.
The DOD Inspector General found that Naval Special Warfare Command failed to identity and treat traumatic brain injuries in personnel.
The Caribbean - bottom line: UDC warns it cannot guarantee daily services at Little Dunn’s River.
- Jamaica Gleaner, 6 hours ago: UDC warns it cannot guarantee daily services at Little Dunn’s River.
The Urban Development Corporation (UDC) says the relevant team has been directed to take steps to facilitate public access to Little Dunn’s River Beach in Ocho Rios, St Ann, in compliance with a court order. However, the UDC indicated that it was not in a position at this time to provide “day-to-day management” of the popular recreational spot, including arrangements for security, lifeguard services, sanitation, maintenance or other amenities ordinarily required for such a facility. The UDC is the state entity that owns the facility.
- Jamaica Gleaner, 6 hours ago: Docs to decide on next steps in response to delayed IDT ruling.
More than 100 junior doctors at the Mandeville Regional Hospital in Manchester stayed off the job on Friday, joining hundreds of colleagues across the island. The junior doctors abstained from work in an effort to pressure the Industrial Disputes Tribunal (IDT) to give a ruling in its overtime and incentive dispute with the Government or outline a timeline for its award.
Central America: no notable developments in the last 48 hours.

SOUTH AMERICA

- Buenos Aires Herald, 2 days ago: Argentine rugby player murdered in Paris honored by French league.

EUROPE
Western Russia - bottom line: Russians attack Izium with drones: five injured.
- Ukrainska Pravda, 3 hours ago: Russians attack Izium with drones: five injured.
Russian forces launched a series of drone strikes on Izium, Kharkiv Oblast, on the morning of 3 October. Five people have been injured.
- Ukrainska Pravda, 6 hours ago: Man, 66, and girl of 8 injured in Russian attack on Hostomel in Kyiv Oblast.
An 8-year-old girl and a man were injured when a Russian strike caused a warehouse fire in Hostomel.
- Ukrainska Pravda, 4 hours ago: Ukraine's General Staff reports strike on UAV launch site and Russian crossing.
Ukraine's defence forces struck a storage and launch site for attack drones, a Russian military command post and a crossing on 2 October and on the night of 2-3 October.
- Ukrainska Pravda, 2 hours ago: Russian relays used to control Shahed drones operating in Kyiv – technology expert Flash.
Presidential adviser Serhii Beskrestnov says Russian MESH radio relays may be operating in Kyiv, allowing Shahed drones to be controlled and their strikes adjusted in real time.
Southern Europe - bottom line: Russia hits major Kyiv bridge, logistics hub in latest attack.
- Politico Europe, one hour ago: Russia hits major Kyiv bridge, logistics hub in latest attack.
Russia struck a key bridge in Kyiv connecting the left and right bank of the Dnipro river overnight Saturday, as Moscow steps up its aerial campaign against Ukraine. Traffic was suspended on the capital’s Northern Bridge and emergency services were deployed to the scene amid damage to the road and trolleybus cables on the crossing, […]
- Balkan Insight, 20 hours ago: Biljana Plavsic, Bosnian Serb War Criminal Who Withdrew Her Remorse.
Plavsic, who died this week, was the only high-ranking woman political leader prosecuted for mass atrocities by the Yugoslav war crimes tribunal. She expressed sorrow for these acts in court – but then changed her mind.
- Balkan Insight, 21 hours ago: Week in Review: Elections and Struggles.
Women get a raw deal at elections in Bosnia, a spy chief’s arrest raises security questions in Albania and protesters challenge war crimes verdicts in Kosovo - plus much more in our selection of this week’s Balkan Insight Premium stories.

Persian Gulf Region - bottom line: IDF targets Yahya Sinwar's successor, Hamas Gaza leader Ali al-Amoudi, in strike.
- Jerusalem Post, just now: IDF targets Yahya Sinwar's successor, Hamas Gaza leader Ali al-Amoudi, in strike.
IDF attack helicopters and tanks struck targets in Gaza on Saturday in an operation aimed at killing Ali al-Amoudi, who succeeded Yahya Sinwar as Hamas's leader in the Gaza Strip.
- Jerusalem Post, just now: One killed several wounded as settler extremists, Palestinians clash across West Bank during Sukkot.
Clashes between settlers and Palestinians were reported across the West Bank during Sukkot, including a deadly shooting in Yasuf and violence linked to the olive harvest.

An Israeli air attack on a residential apartment in Gaza City has killed at least five Palestinians.

- AllAfrica - Conflict, 21 hours ago: Ethiopia: Who Gets to Author Ethiopia's Political Order? Why the Crisis Is About More Than Identity Politics.
[Addis Standard] Addis Abeba -- A familiar explanation of Ethiopia's recurring crises starts with identity: politics organized around nationality can harden boundaries, reward exclusionary mobilization, and expose minorities, migrants, mixed communities, and dissenters to exclusion when democratic protections are weak. International Crisis Group and other scholars have long raised these concerns.

[Daily Trust] Suspected Boko Haram insurgents have ambushed and killed 15 farmers, while abducting three others in Marte Local Government Area of Borno State.

ASIA
South Asia - bottom line: Ethiopia's Tigray rebels abandon regional capital as govt advances.
- Dawn (Pakistan), just now: Ethiopia's Tigray rebels abandon regional capital as govt advances.
Tigray rebels were abandoning their regional capital in northern Ethiopia on Saturday, a local journalist and residents told AFP, as pro-government forces advanced on the city. Fighting erupted on September 23 in northern Ethiopia as the rebel Tigray People’s Liberation Front (TPLF) launched attacks into neighbouring states, raising fears of a return to the devastating 2020-2022 civil war. But federal forces and pro-government militias have pushed them back in recent days and they were heading north towards the regional capital, Mekelle.
- Dawn (Pakistan), one hour ago: 11 terrorists killed during operations in KP, Balochistan: state media.
Security forces killed 11 terrorists during intelligence-based operations (IBOs) in Khyber Pakhtunkhwa and Balochistan, state media reported on Saturday. State-run Radio Pakistan reported that five Fitna al-Khawarij terrorists had been killed during an IBO in KP’s South Waziristan district. Quoting security sources, the report said that security forces were continuing effective operations against Fitna al-Khawarij in KP under the Azm-i-Istehkam vision.
- Dawn (Pakistan), 9 hours ago: Govts should be allowed to complete their terms: CM Maryam.
LAHORE: Punjab Chief Minister Maryam Nawaz has said governments that perform well should be allowed to complete their five-year terms, arguing that the lack of policy continuity in Pakistan remains a major hurdle to development. She was addressing a delegation of the National Command Authority Senior Officers Leadership Course on Thursday, according to an official handout.
- Dawn (Pakistan), 3 hours ago: High school students in Paris' deprived suburbs spark national protest movement.
Maisa, a 17-year-old in a poor Paris suburb who aspires to be an English teacher, joined tens of thousands of other students and their supporters this week in protests that spread across France over dilapidated schools, classroom overcrowding and teacher shortages. At Lycee Le Corbusier school in Aubervilliers, a suburb north of Paris in the Seine-Saint-Denis department, protesters said schools in poor neighborhoods like theirs faced the worst conditions. Last year I took the high school French exam without a French teacher, and teachers have a huge impact,“ Maisa said.
India - bottom line: Pakistan kills 5 TTP militants as violence escalates on Afghanistan border.
- Times of India - Top Stories, one hour ago: Pakistan kills 5 TTP militants as violence escalates on Afghanistan border.
In a decisive operation, Pakistani security forces eliminated five militants affiliated with Tehreek-e-Taliban Pakistan in Khyber Pakhtunkhwa. This mission was executed based on critical intelligence that pinpointed various militant hideouts. Alongside this successful strike, the forces seized a substantial arsenal of weapons and ammunition. This action is a response to the recent surge in violence linked to the TTP, emphasizing the military's ongoing commitment to combatting terrorism in the region.
- Times of India - Top Stories, 7 hours ago: Watch: Hindu temple in US attacked with bricks, windows shattered.
An attack on the Shree Swaminarayan Vadtal Dham Hindu Mandir in Richmond Heights occurred while devotees were present. The incident involved bricks being thrown at the temple, resulting in shattered windows. Surveillance footage is being reviewed by authorities to identify the perpetrator. This potential hate crime coincides with Hindu Heritage Month and upcoming Navratri celebrations.
- NDTV - Top Stories, just now: 'She Was Calm': Neighbour Shares How flydubai Pilot's Wife Reacted To Crisis.
While Captain Smit Machchhar recovers from the attack, his wife’s calm response to neighbours’ messages has highlighted the strength of families who wait, worry and pray for their loved ones to return home.
- Times of India - Top Stories, one hour ago: CM Vijay slams MK Stalin over ‘indecent’ remarks against TVK candidate.
C Joseph Vijay criticized MK Stalin for making derogatory comments about P Sathyabama at an election meeting. He accused the DMK of fostering a violent political culture and disrespecting women. TVK plans to take legal action against Stalin and Udhayanidhi Stalin if offensive remarks continue. A formal complaint was submitted to the chief electoral officer citing body-shaming of the candidate.

Pakistani troops are expected to take over various defensive functions for Saudi Arabia to enable the Middle East country to fight an all-out war aimed at defeating Yemen’s Iran-backed Houthi rebels. According to defence analysts, Pakistani troops are not expected to participate directly in ground offensives against the Houthis being planned by Saudi Arabia and Yemen’s squabbling government factions. The Japanese government on Friday announced additional sanctions against Russia amid the ongoing invasion of Ukraine, targeting a so-called shadow fleet of vessels engaged in transporting sanctioned oil from Russia. Joining international efforts to crack down on sanctions evasion by the fleet, Japan has decided to impose restrictions on the provision of services to 35 vessels, according to the Foreign Ministry. The measures restrict the provision of services including insurance, maritime...

Chinese troops have taken part in a mass multinational exercise in Russia featuring new anti-drone and ground robot systems – drills that Russian state media said “applied lessons” from the Ukraine war. The troops were among more than 47,000 military personnel involved in the Tsentr-2026 – or Centre-2026 – drills in the central western Chelyabinsk region from Monday until Saturday.
